children: ICE New York cocoa fell sharply on Friday to post a 11% weekly loss, while London cocoa registered its third consecutive week of losses.
Raw sugar fell to a three-week low, while coffee rose.
COCOA
* London cocoa
​settled down £318, or 7.5%, at £3,934 per metric ton. The market fell 9% in the week.
* A dealer said this season's surplus was weighing on prices and that there were fears the recent run-up in prices dented demand in the third quarter.
* Elsewhere, rains in West Africa have been sparse of late, but the market is expecting a buildup in supplies at ports as the new marketing season gets underway.

* Ivory Coast has said cocoa shipments are expected to accelerate in the coming weeks as a new marketing system gets underway, with nearly 26,000 tons having already arrived at ports between the season start on September 1 and September 13.
* New York cocoa
fell 7.7% to $5,327 a ton, having hit a 1-1/2-month low of $5,290 earlier.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
​​settled down 0.06 cent, or 0.3%, at 17.36 cents per lb, after setting a three-week low of 17.34 cents. The market lost 4.3% in the week.
* Oil prices edged lower, tempting cane mills to produce more sugar and less of the biofuel ethanol.
* Rains in top grower Brazil are forecast to subside over the next 10 days or so, dealers said, lessening the risk of disruption to crush.
* Elsewhere, China's August sugar imports fell 13.5% to 650,000 tons, data showed.
* In India, meanwhile, the government has relaxed the sugar stockholding limit for bulk consumers from 15 to 30 days and urged traders to pass on lower ex-mill prices to consumers.
* White sugar
was little changed at $508.80 a ton.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
settled up 4 cents, or 1.4%, at $2.805 per lb, its first gain in four sessions. However, it hit a 2-1/2-month low of $2.7505 earlier. Arabica fell 1.8% weekly.
* Coffee is under pressure overall from an increase in ICE arabica stocks, increased Brazilian exports and beneficial weather in Brazil and Vietnam.
* ICE arabica stocks rose by 10,528 bags on Friday to a total of 258,415 bags.
* Robusta coffee
was little changed at $3,396 a ton.
